ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an air-core radio-frequency transformer, with a sinusoidal AC source on the left and the frequency marked as 100 kHz; above the transformer, the mutual inductance M is indicated with an arrow. The port of the secondary winding on the right is open-circuited, and the voltage next to it is marked as 7.3 Vp-p. Below there is a 22 Ω resistor as a current-sensing resistor, the voltage across its two ends is marked as 5.0 Vp-p, and its lower end is grounded. Reasoning: The peak-to-peak voltage on the resistor is 5.0 Vp-p, so the peak-to-peak value of the primary-side current is I1 = 5.0/22 A. The induced voltage of the open-circuited secondary satisfies V2 = ω M I1. Dividing using the same peak-to-peak quantities is sufficient, because the ratio of sinusoidal quantities does not change. The frequency f = 100 kHz, so ω = 2πf = 2π × 100000 rad/s. Substituting gives M = V2/(ω I1) = 7.3 / [(2π × 100000)(5.0/22)] H = (7.3 × 22)/(2π × 100000 × 5.0) H = 5.1119 × 10^-5 H = 51.119 μH. Therefore the mutual inductance is about 51.12 μH, namely about 51.1 μH.
